title: AI regulation takes focus at Abu Dhabi summit
source_used: CNBC Africa (CNN page is a video blurb only; The National also read)
key_facts: CNN page (video) says Becky Anderson spoke with Mistral AI CEO Arthur Mensch about the AI safety debate at Abu Dhabi's AI Everything summit; no transcript.
CNBC Africa: Ai Everything Abu Dhabi opened Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 at ADNEC, a two-day event with 400+ exhibitors, 180+ speakers, 200+ investors managing $100 billion, visitors from 70+ countries.
UAE AI minister Omar Sultan Al Olama said the UAE is training about 80,000 government employees as AI 'super users' able to build agents.
Ahmed Tamim Hisham Al Kuttab, chairman of Abu Dhabi's Department of Government Enablement, opened with a keynote on the goal of the world's first AI-native government by 2027.
Mensch said demand for alternatives to US and Chinese AI is enormous; about 55% of the global economy sits outside both.
The National: Mensch said Mistral may invest in UAE data centres and that sovereign, locally controlled cyber and defence AI matters.
No regulation decision or agreement was reported in the sources read.
quote_evidence: "We've gone on a very aggressive campaign to train around 80,000 government employees, to become super users of AI, being able to build agents and leverage these models."
"Sovereignty matters in that. It's important to be able to wield defence systems without having to ask for permission."
CNN's Becky Anderson speaks to Mistral AI CEO Arthur Mensch about the debate over artificial intelligence safety at Abu Dhabi's AI Everything summit.
why_it_matters_hint: Gulf state pushes AI government adoption and sovereign AI while European AI firm Mistral courts it.
notes: CNN item is a video with a one-line description; no text. Entry built from CNBC Africa and The National (our own entry, no copied text). Nothing was decided on regulation in the sources found; the CNN headline suggests more regulation content than text supports.
